# Selenium (Python bindings)

> The official Python bindings for Selenium WebDriver, maintained by the Selenium
> project. This file ships inside the installed package so that tools reading a
> project's dependencies can find the project's own guidance rather than inferring
> it. The version of the package that contains this file is the version its rules
> describe; read `selenium.__version__` to confirm.

## Documentation

- [Documentation](https://www.selenium.dev/documentation/): task-oriented guides for
  every binding — waits, locators, browser options, Grid, and WebDriver BiDi.
- [Python API reference](https://www.selenium.dev/selenium/docs/api/py/): exact
  signatures, arguments, return types and exceptions for this package.
- [Machine-readable index for the Python API reference](https://www.selenium.dev/selenium/docs/api/py/llms.txt)
- [Deprecated APIs and their replacements](https://www.selenium.dev/selenium/docs/api/py/deprecations.json):
  generated from the source; check an API against this before suggesting it.
- [Changelog](https://github.com/SeleniumHQ/selenium/blob/trunk/py/CHANGES)
- [Issues](https://github.com/SeleniumHQ/selenium/issues)

## Writing Selenium code

These rules correct the patterns that appear most often in code written from older
sources. Each names the release in which the old form stopped being correct.

- Do not set a driver path and do not add a third-party driver manager package.
  Selenium Manager downloads and configures both the browser and its driver, so
  `webdriver.Chrome()` is complete and correct on its own. `executable_path=` was
  removed in 4.10; `Service(ChromeDriverManager().install())` adds a dependency that
  duplicates what Selenium already does. Pass a `Service` only to override a specific
  local binary or a driver log setting.
- Configure the browser with an options object, never with capability dictionaries.
  `desired_capabilities=` was removed in 4.10. Use
  `webdriver.Chrome(options=ChromeOptions())`, and set values with
  `options.add_argument(...)` or `options.set_capability(...)`.
- Locate elements with `By`: `driver.find_element(By.ID, "submit")`. The
  `find_element_by_*` methods were removed in 4.3.
- Wait for a condition, never for a duration. Replace `time.sleep(...)` with
  `WebDriverWait(driver, 10).until(EC.element_to_be_clickable((By.ID, "submit")))`.
  Do not combine `driver.implicitly_wait(...)` with `WebDriverWait`; the two wait
  strategies compound unpredictably.
- Prefer WebDriver BiDi over CDP. `driver.script`, `driver.network`,
  `driver.browsing_context` and `driver.webextension` are cross-browser and stable.
  CDP is Chromium-only and pinned to a browser version.
- Headless mode is an argument, not a property: `options.add_argument("--headless=new")`
  for Chrome and Edge, `options.add_argument("-headless")` for Firefox. The
  `options.headless` property was removed in 4.9.
- End a session with `driver.quit()`, which closes every window and stops the driver
  process. `driver.close()` only closes the current window.

## A complete, current example

```python
from selenium import webdriver
from selenium.webdriver.common.by import By
from selenium.webdriver.support import expected_conditions as EC
from selenium.webdriver.support.wait import WebDriverWait

options = webdriver.ChromeOptions()
options.add_argument("--headless=new")

driver = webdriver.Chrome(options=options)
try:
    driver.get("https://www.selenium.dev/selenium/web/web-form.html")
    driver.find_element(By.NAME, "my-text").send_keys("Selenium")
    driver.find_element(By.CSS_SELECTOR, "button").click()

    message = WebDriverWait(driver, 10).until(EC.visibility_of_element_located((By.ID, "message")))
    assert message.text == "Received!"
finally:
    driver.quit()
```
